text:
kai: Heads up — onboarding a new cloud account (gcp: prod-eu-2) and we're getting a ton of 429s from the network API when creating firewall/security-group style rules. This is preventing the GPU node pools from finishing boot. Anyone seen this pattern before?

infra-bot: [alert] 1809876550 - provider=gcp service=compute.googleapis.com method=firewalls.insert status=429 quotaExceeded

marta: Yep, Google has a per-project create-rate quota on firewall objects. It looks like we're hitting `firewalls.create` rate limits when Terraform does parallel resource creation. The console shows: `You have exceeded your rate limit for firewall rules`.

ashley: Oof. This is for the auto-provisioning path when Dedicated pools spin up GPUs, right? If rules fail the node bootstrap times out and the controller keeps retrying which just amplifies the problem.

kai: Exactly. The node pool creation fails waiting for infra rules -> autoscaler keeps trying -> more API calls -> more 429s. A feedback loop. Region is europe-west2 for these tests.

cloudops: Short-term mitigation: reduce parallelism in Terraform/apply and add exponential backoff on the infra reconcile loop. We can also switch to a 'template first' flow: create a smaller set of shared, permissive rules and reuse them for new pools rather than creating a rule per node pool.

soren: Agree on backoff. Also filing a quota support case with Google is required — they can raise the create-rate limits per project but it takes 24-72h.

ashley: Can someone paste the terraform error block here? I want to grep logs for the exact failure string.

marta: Sure, from the controller logs: 

```
Error: Error creating Firewall: googleapi: Error 429: Rate Limit Exceeded: create requests per minute, rateLimitExceeded
on vpc.tf line 42, in resource "google_compute_firewall" "node_pool_rules":
42: resource "google_compute_firewall" "node_pool_rules" {
```

kai: Workarounds evaluated: 
- throttle Terraform `-parallelism=2` (reduces immediate failures)
- reuse shared firewall rules per cluster (requires a small change to provisioning flow)
- make the controller create rules with jittered backoff instead of immediate retries
- open support case with GCP to increase `firewalls.create` quota

cloudops: I'll open the support case now. Filing as: "compute.googleapis.com - firewall creation rate limit impacting GPU node provisioning". Will request a temporary bump for prod-eu-2 and any related test projects.

infra-bot: [support-case] 1809876589 - Case created with GCP: case id GC-894522. Severity: production impact.

ashley: Thanks. Can we also add an escape hatch — a script that pre-creates a set of 10 standardized rules (ingress/egress & node-authorized ranges) so nodepool bootstrap can skip rule creation entirely? Ops can run it once per project/region.

marta: I can prototype that script today. Will post in #eng-infra once done. It will create rules in series with a 1s sleep between requests to avoid bursts.

soren: Another angle — check if some older CI jobs are tearing things down and re-creating networks in parallel. We should add a global lock key in our infra automation to prevent concurrent mass updates.

kai: Action items: 
- cloudops: escalate and follow up with GC case GC-894522 (ETA: 24h)
- marta: prototype pre-create scripted rules + serial create (ETA: EOD)
- infra: add exponential backoff + reduce default parallelism in provisioning (PR to controller, ETA: tomorrow)
- ops: run pre-create script on prod-eu-2 as temporary fix after script validated

ashley: Marking this P1 for the onboarding flow until the quota bump lands. If you need me to join the support call ping me. :phone: :+1:

kai: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If GC responds we should update the runbook so future onboardings avoid the loop.
